bib.title: Unlimiformer: Long-Range Transformers with Unlimited Length Input
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Appendix F sample outputs (Brothers Karamazov summaries) skimmed, not analysed

question: Can a pretrained encoder-decoder transformer accept inputs of unbounded length, without new weights, by offloading cross-attention to a kNN index over all input tokens?
hypothesis: Letting every cross-attention head retrieve its own top-k keys from the whole input improves long-input generation over truncation, with or without extra training.
contributions: Unlimiformer: wraps any pretrained encoder-decoder and offloads cross-attention to a single kNN index, each head in each decoder layer retrieving its top-k keys
An attention reformulation (h_d W_q W_k^T) h_e^T that allows one index for all heads and layers
Training variants (test-only, early stop, chunked, random-encoded, retrieval, alternating) evaluated on GovReport, SummScreen, BookSum

method.summary: Long inputs are encoded in overlapping chunks by the frozen encoder, keeping the middle half of each chunk's vectors, and indexed in Faiss with dot-product similarity. At each decoding step every cross-attention head queries the index with the reformulated query h_d W_q W_k^T and attends only to its top-k hidden states, k equal to the model context window. Evaluated at test time only and with several training regimes on BART-base and PRIMERA.
method.task: long-document and book summarization (also QA, NLI, query-based summarization)

datasets.name: GovReport (SCROLLS)
datasets.split: SCROLLS splits; test results in Tables 3-4, validation in Table 9
datasets.source: Huang et al. 2021 via Shaham et al. 2022

datasets.name: BookSum-Book
datasets.size: 436 examples; avg 143,301 input tokens, 1294 output; max about 642k tokens

datasets.name: WikiSum (rescraped)
datasets.preprocessing: inputs shorter than 1457 words removed (40th percentile of citation size in original); input paragraphs ranked by TF-IDF

models.name: BART-base
models.layers: inferred: 6 decoder layers (Table 8 lists up to 6 (all))
models.hidden: inferred: 1024 hidden used in memory example (Sec 2.3); BART-base hidden not stated

models.name: Memorizing Transformers (approximation)
models.architecture: kNN attention in a single decoder layer, gate g set to 1

other.note: authors approximated it because the public implementation is not officially supported

training.seq_len: truncate longest inputs, generally to 16k tokens, for long-range methods; 1024 for low-cost methods
training.regularisation: random-encoded batches alternated with retrieval batches act as regularisation
training.hardware: single 48-GB A6000 (32 GB RAM, 16 CPUs for timing)
training.compute: total did not exceed approximately 116 days on one 48-GB A6000
training.wall_clock: SLED and retrieval training for GovReport about 10 days

other.hyperparameters: 'using the hyperparameter settings from SLED (Ivgi et al., 2022) and early stopping'; values not restated
other.variants: +test Unlimiformer; +early stop w/ Unlimiformer; Train chunked (non-overlapping 1024-token chunks as separate examples); Random-encoded; Retrieval; Alternating

inference.samples: single run per setting; timing averaged over 3 runs
inference.retrieval: kNN (Faiss) over encoder last-layer hidden states of the single input, dot-product similarity; top-k per head per layer with k equal to context window (1024 for BART); overlapping chunks, middle half of each chunk's vectors kept; GPU index used for inputs over 500k tokens on 48 GB GPUs, CPU index otherwise slower

parameters.k: equal to model context window size (stated Sec 2.3)

other.faiss_gpu_limit: Faiss GPU index does not support retrieving more than 2048 neighbours, so CPU index needed for windows over 2048

metrics.name: BERTScore F1
metrics.definition: vanilla limited to 512 tokens; facebook/bart-large-mnli (1024) used for GovReport and ScriptSumm; BookSum Longformer-large-4096 variant tried and rejected as non-discriminative

metrics.name: Entity Mention Recall (EntMent)
metrics.definition: recall of unique gold-summary named entities (SpaCy en_core_web_lg) in candidate

eval.protocol: single run per setting, no significance tests; early stopping on validation

availability.data: WikiSum training subset and scraping code released

results.claim: Adding Unlimiformer at test time only to a standard-finetuned BART-base raises GovReport ROUGE-1.
results.setup: BART-base (139M), GovReport test, ROUGE-1, single trained model per setting; truncated-input finetuning, Unlimiformer injected at inference only
results.table: Table 3, rows BARTbase Standard finetuning vs +test Unlimiformer, GovReport ROUGE-1

results.claim: Alternating-trained Unlimiformer on BART-base beats SLED and Memorizing Transformers on GovReport.
results.setup: BART-base, GovReport test, long-range (16k-truncated, batch size 1) training, alternating training strategy; ROUGE-1
results.table: Table 4, row BARTbase Unlimiformer (this work), GovReport ROUGE-1; SLED 54.7; Memorizing transformers 55.2; Standard finetuning 48.7

results.claim: On BookSum, test-time Unlimiformer on BART-base lowers ROUGE-1 slightly relative to truncating to the first 1024 tokens.
results.setup: BART-base, BookSum-Book test, avg input about 143k tokens; truncation baseline vs +test Unlimiformer
results.note: ROUGE-2 7.7 vs 7.6 and ROUGE-L 15.4 vs 15.3 are marginally higher with Unlimiformer; only ROUGE-1 is lower.
results.table: Table 5, rows BARTbase Standard finetuning vs +test Unlimiformer, ROUGE 1

results.claim: Test-time Unlimiformer roughly doubles entity mention recall on BookSum for BART-base.
results.setup: BART-base, BookSum-Book test; EntMent = fraction of unique gold entities (SpaCy en_core_web_lg) mentioned in candidate
results.note: Text names the 'Early stop w/ Unlimiformer' row; Table 5 gives 21.9 for both +test and +early stop rows of BART-base.
results.quote: even adding Unlimiformer only at test time without costly training (Early stop w/ Unlimiformer) doubles the entity recall compared to the base model

results.claim: PRIMERA entity recall on BookSum rises from 11.6 to 25.5 with retrieval-trained Unlimiformer.
results.quote: Further, Unlimiformer improves EntMent in the base PRIMERA from 11.6 to 25.5 in Unlimiformer+PRIMERA.

results.claim: Unlimiformer attends to the top-k keys, which cover more than 99% of attention mass in preliminary experiments.
results.setup: preliminary experiments, no setup given (model, dataset not stated)
results.note: Preliminary result; no table or setup reported.
results.quote: we found that the top-k attention keys cover more than 99% of the attention mass

results.claim: Index memory is one vector per input token: 2GB for 1,000,000 tokens at 16-bit, hidden size 1024.
results.setup: 16-bit floats, hidden size 1024, single index shared across all heads and layers
results.quote: Using 16-bit floats and hidden states of size 1024, this requires only 2GB of memory for 1,000,000 input tokens.

results.claim: Chunked training plus test-time Unlimiformer gives the largest low-cost GovReport gain.
results.setup: BART-base, GovReport test, training cost same as standard finetuning (Train chunked +test Unlimiformer: 53.4 vs 46.2 for Train chunked alone)
results.note: Gain is measured against the Train chunked row (46.2), not against standard finetuning (48.7).
results.quote:
results in the most significant gains: 7.2 ROUGE-1 and 3
BERTScore points improvements

results.claim: Retrieval training costs about 1.9x and random-encoded training about 2.9x the GPU-time of baseline training per epoch; Unlimiformer inference costs about 4.5x.
results.setup: BookSum, single 48 GB A6000, 32 GB RAM, 16 CPUs, mean of 3 runs
results.table: Table 7, row Unlimiformer inference, column Relative GPU-time (1.89 retrieval training, 2.87 random-encoded training)

results.claim: GPU memory with Unlimiformer is constant in the number of layers it is applied to (about 7.3 GB for BART) versus 1.61 GB for normal inference.
results.setup: BART, BookSum inputs, some over 500,000 tokens

results.claim: On WikiSum, where paragraphs were ranked by TF-IDF, Unlimiformer did not beat the first 1024 tokens of the sorted input.
results.setup: WikiSum rescraped subset (10,000 train, 1,000 val, 1,000 test), BART-base; no numbers given in text
results.note: Authors also note possible pretraining contamination of the baseline (BART saw Wikipedia).
results.quote:
Unlimiformer did not improve over a baseline that uses only the first 1024 tokens of this
sorted input

results.claim: Retrieved keys are spread across the whole BookSum input; median retrieved location is about 50% of the way through.
results.quote:
for all models, the median location of a retrieved
key was between 49.73% and 49.87% of the way
through the input document

results.claim: Only 43.5% to 64.5% of input tokens are retrieved at least once on BookSum.
results.setup: BookSum test; 43.5% for test-time-only, 64.5% for alternating-training model
results.quote:
from 43.5% of all tokens for the test-time-only Unlimiformer to 64.5% of all tokens for the alternating-
training model

results.claim: On QASPER, Unlimiformer improves BART-base F1 from 22.0 to 27.5; on NarrativeQA from 15.5 to 18.5; Contract NLI and QMSum are about flat.
results.setup: BART-base with alternating training, SCROLLS validation splits
results.table: Table 6, rows BARTbase Standard finetuning vs Unlimiformer, column QASPER F1 (NarrativeQA 15.5 to 18.5; Contract NLI EM 77.5 to 77.7; QMSum ROUGE-2 8.7 to 8.0)

results.claim: Total compute for the paper did not exceed about 116 days on one 48-GB A6000; SLED and retrieval training on GovReport took about 10 days each.
results.quote:
did not exceed approximately 116
days of time on a single 48-GB A6000

results.claim: Inference time grows sublinearly with input length, though encoding the full input makes Unlimiformer inference costlier than truncation.
results.setup: BookSum, wall-clock per example, Fig 4 (values read from figure only)
results.quote:
the total GPU-time required increases sublinearly
with input length

limits: Training input length bounded by GPU memory (truncated to about 16k tokens at training)
CPU-offloaded index gives higher test-time latency; GPU index worked to over 500k tokens only on 48GB GPUs
BookSum ROUGE and BERTScore barely separate truncated baseline from Unlimiformer; EntMent used as proxy, hallucination judged by manual inspection of one example
Single run per setting, no variance or significance reported
Encoder-decoder models up to 447M only; LLaMA-2 support mentioned but not evaluated
No comparison against chunk-level RAG or retrieve-then-summarise pipelines

terms.definition: the fraction of gold entities mentioned in the candidate summary
